misconceptions.misconception: Believing high leverage creates free profits without downside risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Because entering a futures position requires zero initial investment, both the futures price F0 and the strike K must be discounted to the present in put-call parity: c + K*e^(-r*T) = p + F0*e^(-r*T) ([fact-03]).

misconceptions.misconception: Believing high leverage creates free profits without downside risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: In risk-neutral valuation, a futures contract has zero drift and behaves mathematically like an asset providing a continuous dividend yield equal to the risk-free rate (q = r) ([fact-04]).

misconceptions.misconception: Believing high leverage creates free profits without downside risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Net trading profit must subtract the initial option premium compounded at the risk-free rate (Profit = Payoff - Premium paid * e^(r*T)); failing to do so creates an illusion of riskless gains ([fact-11]).

activeRecallQuiz.scenario: Consider a European call option on crude oil futures where current futures price F0 = $50, strike K = $50, risk-free rate r = 6% per annum, futures volatility sigma = 30%, and time to maturity T = 0.75 years. The calculated call premium is c = $4.87.
activeRecallQuiz.question: 1) What underlying positions and cash adjustments occur when this futures call option is exercised? 2) Why do financial institutions prefer Fischer Black's model over standard Black-Scholes-Merton for commodities and interest rates?
activeRecallQuiz.correctAnswer: Correctly identifying the downside risk and margin constraints.

coreTakeaways: Futures options deliver underlying futures positions plus cash adjustments upon exercise and are widely preferred over spot options due to superior liquidity and margin netting ([fact-01], [fact-02]).
Fischer Black's (1976) model prices futures options by treating futures contracts as assets with continuous dividend yield equal to the risk-free rate (q = r) ([fact-04], [fact-05]).

American futures calls can be optimally exercised early when futures prices are high and expected to decline, while futures-style options eliminate upfront premiums via daily mark-to-market margining ([fact-09], [fact-10]).
